_meta.description: Mix two of three colors to match the target. Continuous difficulty, additive & subtractive mixing, surprise inversion stages, dynamic music, turn-based multiplayer, and iMessage play. No ads, no tracking.
a-more-flexible-ipad.4f5465: A more flexible iPad experience and a round of polish
a-procedural-bed-whose.790c9d: A procedural bed whose intensity and layers scale with difficulty and streak, with a major↔minor swap and a stinger on every inversion.
a-simplified-tap-to.f64f05: A simplified tap-to-mix mode on Apple Watch for a quick round anywhere. No ads. No tracking. Ever.
additive-mode-adds-light.97d9ac: Additive mode adds light toward white; subtractive mode multiplies pigment toward black. Two ways to think about every mix.
all-four-ipad-orientations.19b44c: All four iPad orientations are supported and the window resizes freely in Split View, Stage Manager, and iPad windowing — the mix board keeps every bubble reachable at any window size.
an-interactive-walk-through.b0eebb: An interactive walk-through replaces the old guide — you learn light mixing, paint mixing, and inversions by actually playing a few guided rounds, not watching a video.
and-keep-an-eye.1690fb: And keep an eye out for inversions: every so often the game flips light↔paint mid-run, changing the badge and the whole theme. Solve the first round after a flip to earn a life.
are-there-ads-iaps.46a41b: Are there ads, IAPs, or subscriptions?
built-in-24-hours.f64269: Built in 24 Hours, Reborn a Decade Later
co-op-builds-one.fbc5f1: Co-op builds one shared streak; competitive races the exact same seeded puzzles. Asynchronous via Game Center — play when you're free.
each-round-shows-a.06e3e3: Each round shows a target color and three bubbles. Drag two bubbles together and they glob into liquid glass — one pair, and only one, reproduces the target. While you have previews the glob shows the mixed color; once they run out, you read it and commit on feel.
early-on-globbing-two.2a0822: Early on, globbing two bubbles previews the mixed color — a couple of peeks per round. Deeper in, the previews fade to none and it's pure color reading.
eight-things-every-tri.6d48ac: Eight things every Tri-Add player learns to love
every-correct-mix-is.40441b: Every correct mix is a level. The colors get subtler and the help fades the deeper you go — climb as far as you can.
every-correct-mix-is.8f619d: Every correct mix is a level. The difficulty curve is invisible — colors quietly get subtler and the help fades the deeper you go — so it always feels like one more.
get-it-right-and.21b298: Get it right and you level up. Get it wrong and you lose a life. Perfect, confident matches score the most.
ipad-any-way-you.3a62ad: iPad, Any Way You Hold It
iphone-and-ipad-universal.8a8058: iPhone and iPad (universal — one purchase covers both), plus a simplified mode on Apple Watch. Built and tuned on iPhone 17 Pro Max.
is-this-the-same.7cd7e3: Is this the same Tri-Add from years ago?
light-additive-mixing-starts.3da1d7: Light (additive) mixing starts from black and adds toward white — red light + green light makes yellow. Paint (subtractive) mixing starts from white and multiplies toward black — cyan + yellow makes green. Tri-Add teaches both, then flips between them mid-game.
mix-two-of-three.bfa75d: Mix two of three colors to match the target. The difficulty climbs the longer you play, the music swells with your streak, and every so often the rules flip — additive light-mixing becomes subtractive paint-mixing, and the whole screen changes with it. A 2014 classic, rebuilt for 2026.
no-tracking-no-ads.9ce4d2: No tracking. No ads. No in-app purchases.
no-tri-add-is.f4c2a1: No. Tri-Add is a one-time $4.99 purchase. No ads, no tracking, no in-app purchases, no subscriptions — every mode included.
open-the-tri-add.a03afa: Open the Tri-Add iMessage app in a conversation, pick co-op or versus, and take your turn. Send the bubble; your friend taps it, plays their round inside Messages, and sends it back. The match lives entirely in your thread.
original-game-by-austin.1f7b90: Original game by Austin Buck & Blaine Miller · Name by Crystal Buck · © Blaine Miller. All rights reserved.
ready-for-ios-27.75e4d6: ✓ Ready for iOS 27 / iPadOS 27 / watchOS 27
send-a-tri-add.255603: Send a Tri-Add bubble. Your friend takes their turn right inside Messages and sends it back. Co-op or versus, one bubble at a time.
the-achievements-list-in.32e0ce: The achievements list in Settings now shows each badge’s actual Game Center artwork — locked badges appear desaturated with a lock, so you can see exactly what you’re chasing.
the-mix-flips-additive.013d9e: The mix flips additive↔subtractive mid-run, with an interrupting animation, a persistent indicator, and a Light/Dark theme flip you can't miss.
then-take-it-online.855bc1: Then take it online: turn-based co-op builds a shared streak, competitive races the same seeded puzzles, and you can even play inside an iMessage bubble.
there-s-no-timer.9a2185: There's no timer — the colors get subtler as your level climbs and the preview "help" fades — two peeks early, then one, then none. A built-in perceptual floor keeps every color visibly distinct, even at the top.
this-version-is-a.56030d: This version is a complete, ground-up rebuild more than a decade later — modern tooling, modern polish, and a few long-wished-for features to make it more fun — staying faithful to the spirit of that time and the fun we shared.
tri-add-isn-t.3128a7: Tri-Add isn't sold on the App Store in the European Union — under the EU Digital Services Act, selling there requires publishing a trader listing with personal contact details, which I've opted out of as an independent developer. It's available in every other App Store territory.
tri-add-started-as.2d10b0: Tri-Add started as a late-night idea right after high school — an offhand "what if" one evening between friends. By the next day it was a whole app. Austin Buck and Blaine Miller built the original in about 24 hours: an idea one night, a shipped game the next, fueled by friendship and the fun of making something together. Crystal Buck gave it its name.
what-devices-does-it.b7b7b0: What devices does it run on?
what-s-the-difference.666d2f: What's the difference between light and paint mixing?
yes-it-s-a.3a6fc5: Yes — it's a relaunch of the 2014 original by Austin Buck & Blaine Miller (named by Crystal Buck), rebuilt from scratch in modern Swift. If you owned it before, it's the same app on the App Store, and your old Game Center achievements still count.
